{{< include ../exercise-header.qmd >}}


::: {#exr-owl-sing-mattress}
For some strange, textbook reason you are in a closed room with no windows. You have been there so long that you don't know what day of the year it is. You wonder what the temperature is like outside.

Here are four shapes of relative probability functions that take temperature as input.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| layout-ncol: 2
prior <- function(temp) {
  dnorm(temp, mean = 55, sd = 15) / dnorm(55, mean = 55, sd = 15)
} 

make_temperature_plot <- function(fname) {
  slice_plot(fname(temp) ~ temp,
  domain(temp = 0:100)) |>
  gf_theme(theme_minimal(base_size = 12)) |>
  gf_labs(x = "Temperature", y = "Relative probability")
}



winter <- function(temp) {
  dnorm(temp, mean = 30, sd = 10) / dnorm(30, mean = 30, sd = 10)
}

summer <- function(temp) {
  dnorm(temp, mean = 75, sd = 10) / dnorm(75, mean = 75, sd = 10)
}

fall_spring <- function(temp) {
  dnorm(temp, mean = 45, sd = 10) / dnorm(45, mean = 45, sd = 10)
}

make_temperature_plot(fall_spring) |> gf_labs(title = "Function A")

make_temperature_plot(prior) |> gf_labs(title = "Function B")

make_temperature_plot(summer) |> gf_labs(title = "Function C")

make_temperature_plot(winter) |> gf_labs(title = "Function D")
```

i. Which of the four functions best represents a sensible *prior* belief about the temperature?

```{mcq}
#| label: D12-xxxx-i
#| inline: true
1. A [hint: too narrow]
2. B [correct]
3. C [hint: too narrow]
4. D [hint: too narrow]
```

Eager to know more about the time of year, you ask to have a thermometer read-out installed which shows the outside temperature.

-----

ii. Which of the four plots shows a sensible *likelihood* for temperature under the hypothesis that it is either spring or fall?

```{mcq}
#| label: D12-xxxx-ii
#| inline: true
1. A [correct]
2. B 
3. C 
4. D 
```

-----

iii. What is the best of the following criterion for judging which of the four functions is suitable for the *prior*?

```{mcq}
#| label: D12-xxxx-iii
1. It should be taller than the others.
2. It should cover only a narrow range of temperatures.
3. It should cover a broad range of temperatures. [correct]
4. It should never have a negative value. [hint: This is true of all relative probability functions.]
```


-----

iv. Which of the four plots shows a sensible *likelihood* for temperature under the hypothesis that it is summer?

```{mcq}
#| label: D12-xxxx-iv
#| inline: true
1. A 
2. B 
3. C [correct]
4. D 
```


:::
